t: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–112, $37,000,000 are rescinded. Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–333, $55,000,000 are rescinded.

fable.w: This section only rescinds previously appropriated funds from two public laws. No outside party such as states, the public, or experts is consulted or involved in any federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. No tempting contrary reading arises, since the text is purely a budgetary rescission.
fable.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–112, $37,000,000 are rescinded.

opus.w: This provision only cancels specific amounts of funds appropriated under two earlier public laws. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government, any consultation, hearing, comment period, or rulemaking. So it does not meet the definition of participation.
opus.b: This section only rescinds appropriated funds. Nothing in it involves outside parties, consultation, hearings, rulemaking, or a right to sue. There is no tempting reading that would make it count as participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply rescinds specific amounts of appropriated funds. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making this budgetary decision. There are no advisory committees, comment periods, or hearings mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–112, $37,000,000 are rescinded. Of the funds made available under this heading in Public Law 103–333, $55,000,000 are rescinded.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that rescinding funds is a "decision" that affects the public, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation in that decision. It is a unilateral legislative action regarding budget allocations.
